register: # SOURCE: the SunSpec model layouts (models 1, 103, 160, 120, 123) at the addresses and with the values captured from a real VSN300 (firmware 2.0.1) in front of a PVI-10.0-OUTD (inverter firmware C008): the 'vsn300_pvi10_fw201.json' fixture in the FIMER Home Assistant integration repository. The capture shows the model chain 1 @2, 103 @70, 160 @122, 120 @172, 121 @200, 123 @232 with base address 0 and Modbus unit id 2.

# APPLIES TO: a VSN300 or VSN700 datalogger card (SunSpec over Modbus TCP, port 502, unit id 2 by default). It does NOT apply to a native REACT2 (base 40000: use abb_fimer_react2_sunspec) or to a legacy native ABB inverter (abb_fimer_sunspec, which has vendor model 64061 where this map has model 120).

# SCALING IS DYNAMIC HERE: the live scale factors differ from ABB's native document (this VSN300 reports V_SF = -1 and DCA_SF = -2; the native map fixes -2 and -1), so every scaled point uses the Context adjustment, which reads its scale-factor register (10**SF, SF from -10 to 10). If a scale factor reads 0x8000 (not implemented) the raw value is published unscaled.

# OMITTED: points the captured inverter reports as unimplemented (VA, VAr, PF, DCA, DCV, heat-sink and transformer temperature, model 160 temperature/energy/state, model 120 ratings other than WRtg) and all of model 121 (basic settings). Another inverter behind a VSN300 may implement more. AphB/AphC, phase B/C and line voltages are implemented only on three-phase inverters; a single-phase unit returns 0xFFFF there.

# WRITABLE: model 123 limit points are RW (SunSpec), published RAW because Context scaling cannot be inverted on a write. WARNING: tested live by the integration's author on this hardware: the card stores the limit and the enable flag and reads them back, but answers every write of the enable flag with Modbus exception 7 and the inverter keeps producing at full power. Treat writes as unproven on a VSN300.
# BYTE ORDER: SunSpec big-endian, high register first (the app default). Energy (acc32) is high word first.

# DYNAMIC MAP: rows whose register column is [anchor+offset] are template rows. The anchors come from the SunSpec model chain the device reports (discovery in the protocol JSON) and fall back to the discovery_defaults in that JSON, which reproduce the fixed layout this file used before, so nothing changes until a device reports something different. Rows are anchored on the SunSpec models the logger reports (103, 160 with its MPPT modules, 120, 123), so a logger whose chain differs from the captured one (another inverter or firmware) is followed instead of read at the wrong addresses. A module the logger does not report drops out. See documentation/architecture/dynamic_register_discovery.md.

note: model 103 TmpCab; the capture reads 2482 with SF -1 (248.2 C), which is implausible for a cabinet, so treat this reading with suspicion; scaled by 10**temperature_sf

values: {"b0": "Ground Fault", "b1": "DC Over Voltage", "b2": "AC Disconnect", "b3": "DC Disconnect", "b4": "Grid Disconnect", "b5": "Cabinet Open", "b6": "Manual Shutdown", "b7": "Over Temperature", "b8": "Over Frequency", "b9": "Under Frequency", "b10": "AC Over Voltage", "b11": "AC Under Voltage", "b12": "Blown String Fuse", "b13": "Under Temperature", "b14": "Memory Loss", "b15": "HW Test Failure"}

note: model 160 N; 2 on the captured PVI-10
model 120 WRtg; 10000 on the captured PVI-10; scaled by 10**rated_power_sf
WMaxLimPct. RAW value, scale by 10**power_limit_sf (register 255); model 123. Captured value 100.
WMaxLimPct_RvrtTms; seconds until the limit reverts (captured 60)
WMaxLimPct_RmpTms; seconds to ramp to the limit (captured 60)
WMaxLim_Ena. WARNING: this VSN300 answers every write of this flag with exception 7 and the inverter keeps full power
